_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: 'ServerProbe treats a body containing 'jsonrpc' as Answered and does not classify 401 as transient, yet the endpoint demonstrably returns exactly that instantly — so the verdict contradicts the endpoint's real behaviour.' Filed as a probe-verdict defect and the root-cause mechanism behind the observed --restart failure.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: That diagnosis was refuted by the project's own follow-up investigation, documented in docs/work/2026-08-21-restart-probe-and-reingest-stale-chunks-plan.md (written between the 1.29.0 and this run): a unit test pinning exactly the claimed shape (ATokenGated401CarryingAJsonRpcBody_ReportsAnswered) passes on the code as it stood — 'the verdict logic was never the problem'. The REAL, separate defect (fixed by #415/PR#415, 'the probe's per-attempt bound is retryable, so the retry is real') is that a per-attempt timeout surfaces as TaskCanceledException, which the retry predicate does not match, so the probe spends its one real attempt against its most likely failure mode. But #415's own commit message states outright: 'NOT claimed: that this explains the 1.29.0 checklist symptom... a clean reproduction of the failing sequence cycled correctly [even before the fix]... the checklist failure remains unexplained.' The plan doc's own words: 'a reason that is right about the outcome and wrong about the cause is exactly what this project's checklist skill warns rots first.'
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: docs/work/2026-08-21-restart-probe-and-reingest-stale-chunks-plan.md lines ~24-65 ('First diagnosis, and why it was wrong' / 'Not proven — that this caused the checklist symptom'); commit 27a8ab4b's message; commit 53397cd9 ('H18 handoff declined with verified reasons — stays open, flagged for owner routing').
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: This run's own item 2 (server-lifecycle) initially made the SAME mistake in its first draft — crediting #415 with fixing the 1.29.0 symptom and calling the old fail verdict 'contradicted' — before this cross-check caught it. Corrected in item 2 above: this run's --restart test is a genuine pass for the mechanism it actually exercised, but is NOT evidence that the original 1.29.0 symptom is explained or fixed; that remains formally open per the project's own tracking (H18/O5). A future run should not re-close this from a single successful --restart call.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: Filed as a real defect ('a re-ingested file leaves its previous chunks behind') needing an issue.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: Not wrong — corroborated. Re-verified live on this build (see item 6 above): still present, unfixed. Recording here only to close the loop: docs/work/2026-08-21-restart-probe-and-reingest-stale-chunks-plan.md ('Defect B') independently traced the exact same root cause (FileIngestor's direct memory_ingest_file path never runs the watch/repair paths' delete-by-source-path step) and proposed a fix, but per commit 53397cd9 the corresponding PR was deferred/declined for this cycle ('H18... stays open, flagged for owner routing'), so it is still open, not silently dropped.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: docs/work/2026-08-21-restart-probe-and-reingest-stale-chunks-plan.md lines 108-195; src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Ingestion/FileIngestor.cs (InsertChunksAsync, no delete step) vs src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sqlite/Memory/SqliteMemoryStore.Replace.cs (ReplaceCoreAsync, has one).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: No correction needed to the 1.29.0 verdict itself — flagging this so a future run knows the defect is tracked (owner routing O5), not that two independent 'checklist found a bug' events with no connection between them.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: tools/call memory_search query="an antique navigation instrument gleaming in candle-glow inside a craftsman's loft" (semantic, zero literal overlap) ; tools/call memory_search query="reset your password account settings Security" (literal-overlap control) -- both against a 4-entry bank (astrolabe note, an unrelated password-reset note, a technical decision note, a sextant note)
items.evidence:
IMPORTANT CAVEAT SURFACED MID-RUN: the first run of this item scored a 'pass' against a bank holding only the ONE just-written entry and NO configured embedding provider (embedding.provider unset, entries.embed_state='pending', embedding blob NULL, vec_entries had no row for it) -- a corpus-of-one always returns its lone entry regardless of true relevance, which is exactly the weak-check trap this skill warns against, and with no embedding at all the 'match' could not have been a real vector hit. Caught this by adding a gibberish query (returned empty, ruling out return-everything) then a real distractor entry and comparing two different queries' full ranked lists, which came back byte-identical in order and RRF score -- traced the scores to the documented rrfK=60 position formula (1/(60+rank), normalized to rank1=1.0), which explained the IDENTICAL SCORES as expected RRF behavior but not the identical ORDER.
Activated the memory embedding engine for real (`ai-raccoon model set local`), drained via memory_embed_pending, confirmed via ?mode=ro that all 4 entries flipped to embed_state='embedded' with distinct unit-norm 384-dim embedding blobs (verified via a Python struct.unpack sanity check: sumsq~=1.0 per row, vectors not identical to each other).
Re-ran with real embeddings: the semantic query (zero literal overlap with astrolabe content) now returns astrolabe rank1, distractor/decision/sextant below it. The literal-overlap control query ('reset your password account settings Security') correctly REORDERS: the password-reset distractor now ranks 1, astrolabe drops to rank3 -- proving the ranking is genuinely query-sensitive, not a fixed/cached order.
items.observed-result: Once a real embedding engine is actually activated, hybrid search correctly discriminates: a semantic-only query (no literal overlap) surfaces the relevant entry over three distractors, and a literal-overlap query correctly promotes a different entry -- both legs are live. Separately: `ai-raccoon model set local` is NOT run automatically on a fresh bank; every write stays deferred ('pending', unembedded) until a provider is explicitly configured, and a naive checklist run against a fresh, unconfigured scratch bank with a single entry can score this item 'pass' for the wrong reason (corpus-of-one, not real retrieval). Recording this as a process note for future runs, not a product defect: FileIngestor.cs's own comment already documents 'nothing embeds yet' for an unconfigured provider (docs/adr/0063) -- the deferred-embedding behavior is intentional.
items.acceptance-reason: Re-verified against a real, multi-entry, actually-embedded bank with both a clean semantic probe and a literal-overlap control that reorders the ranking -- the corpus-of-one weak-check trap from the first attempt was caught and superseded before accepting this item.

items.expected-result: the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)

items.evidence:
refuse -> isError:true 'invalid-params: This looks like tool output rather than a question... Refused query: [IMPORTANT: Background process completed normally. Command: dotnet build]'

items.acceptance-reason: All three tiers behave as ADR-0040/0041 specify; the refuse tier's exact trigger shape was verified against QueryGuardPolicy.cs source rather than assumed from the prior run's looser description ('a Hermes notification').

items.expected-result: model set code local against a directory holding a non-768 manifest refuses with an actionable error naming 768 (server-side, not just CLI); a missing manifest surfaces the loader's own error; activating the real downloaded code-daemon-embed-v1 (ai-raccoon model download) succeeds and writes embedding.codeModel/codeEngine. The refusal legs must be run live; if the 187 MB download is infeasible in this run, the activation leg is 'substituted' naming the BDD/integration instrument.
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch> --port 59977 model set code local <non768-manifest-dir> ; ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch> --port 59977 model set code local <missing-manifest-dir> ; ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch> model download faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1 --yes
items.evidence:
SAFETY NOTE (self-caught mid-run after a coordinator warning about another lane's near-miss): the first pass at these two refusal legs omitted --port and so dialed the default 7721 instead of this run's own ephemeral server -- verified nothing was written to the scratch bank's settings table either way (no code% rows), and PID 7721's incumbent server (pid 57904, running since before this task started) was confirmed still alive and undisturbed afterward, but both legs were re-run with explicit --port 59977 against this run's own server before accepting the results; the two outputs below are the --port-59977 (confirmed-correct-server) run, byte-identical to the first pass.
non-768 leg -> exit 15: 'ai-raccoon: Manifest '<dir>' declares 1024-dimension embeddings, but the code corpus's vec_code index is fixed at 768 dimensions — there is no dimension-reconcile phase for code, unlike the memory bank. Point 'model set code local' at a manifest with dimensions: 768.'
missing-manifest leg -> exit 15: 'ai-raccoon: Configured embedding model directory '<dir>' has no ai-raccoon.manifest.json. ... run 'ai-raccoon model download <repo-id>' to create one, or point embedding.model at a .onnx file for the legacy path.'
Real-download leg -> FAILS IMMEDIATELY (not a 10-minute timeout): after resolving the tree and fetching config.json/tokenizer_config.json (~1.3s total), exits 15 with 'ai-raccoon: tokenizer_config.json has no added_tokens_decoder object; special-token ids are never guessed — cannot pin them.' Verified against the REAL faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1 HF repo directly (curl): its tokenizer_config.json is genuinely 166 bytes, {tokenizer_class, model_max_length, bos_token, eos_token, unk_token, pad_token} — no added_tokens_decoder, no tokenizer.json (404), no special_tokens_map.json. config.json DOES carry numeric bos_token_id=0/eos_token_id=2/pad_token_id=1 (standard xlm-roberta) but the planner (ModelDownloadPlanner.SpecialTokenIds, src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Embedding/Download/ModelDownloadPlanner.cs:255-299) only ever reads tokenizer_config.json's added_tokens_decoder, never config.json's *_token_id fields — and even a config.json fallback would not resolve unk_token_id, which the repo declares nowhere numerically. This is a genuine, permanent, external-repo blocker (by design, ADR D1 'never guess special-token ids'), not a timeout.
items.observed-result: Both refusal legs behave exactly as specified, confirmed live against this run's own server. The real-model activation leg cannot be exercised in ANY amount of wall time against the actual faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1 repo as it is published today — the download planner correctly and deliberately refuses rather than guessing, so this is working-as-designed against an incompatible real-world repo, not a bug to patch (deliberately not attempted: loosening D1's guarantee is an owner-level product decision, and even a config.json bos/eos/pad fallback would still fail on the missing unk_token_id).
items.acceptance-reason: Refusal legs: substituted->no, both PASS and accepted, re-confirmed on the correct server after a self-caught port-safety issue. Real-activation leg: substituted, naming CodeCorpusSteps.cs's BDD scenarios (docs/features/code-corpus/code-corpus.feature, 'model set code local accepts a 768-dimension manifest' and the activation-writes-embedding.codeModel/codeEngine scenarios) plus tests/AiRaccoon.Tests's CodeReindexJobTests as the instrument that exercises real activation against a manifest fixture with valid (if placeholder-hashed) files, since the actual HTTP-downloadable model cannot be pinned today. NOT accepted as fully proven live — this is a real, reportable product gap (see report): faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1, the exact model ADR-0087/0088 target, cannot be downloaded via the shipped 'ai-raccoon model download' command at all.

ignored.md
excluded_dir
' at ingest root, holding thing.secret.cs (code), ignored.md (memory), excluded_dir/nested.py (code, nested), and kept_dir/kept.md (memory, control) ; memory_ingest_directory over the root ; memory_ingest_file directly on ignored.md and on thing.secret.cs

directory ingest -> {"scanned":1} (only the control file). sqlite (?mode=ro): entries.source_file LIKE '%ignoreroot%' -> exactly 1 row, kept_dir/kept.md. code_entries.source_file LIKE '%ignoreroot%' -> 0 rows (thing.secret.cs and the nested excluded_dir/nested.py both absent from the code corpus).

The non-ignored sibling (kept.md) ingested normally as the negative control.
items.acceptance-reason: All four clauses (both-corpora directory exclusion, bare-dir-name subtree exclusion, explicit single-file ignore, negative control) verified live in one continuous fixture.

items.expected-result: memory_watch_add of a path nested inside an existing watch is REJECTED naming the covering watch; adding a broader watch over an existing narrower one prunes the narrower (result lists it); equal-path re-add is an idempotent no-op reporting absorbedBy.
items.command: memory_watch_add(watchdir) [already registered from file-watch-status item] ; memory_watch_add(watchdir/nested_sub) [nested] ; memory_watch_add(scratchpad) [broader, covers watchdir] ; memory_watch_add(scratchpad) again [equal re-add]
items.observed-result: All three overlap rules behave exactly as specified: a nested watch is refused and names the covering watch; a broader watch prunes the narrower one it swallows and reports it; re-adding the identical path is a true no-op (empty pruned) that reports absorbedBy pointing at itself.
items.acceptance-reason: All three overlap shapes exercised live in sequence against the same registered watch.
